To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
participation in BPCI for medical conditions was associated, at three years, with a reduction in total spending for episodes of care, with no changes in mortality.

longer term participation in a large national programme to bundle payments for four common medical comorbidities in the United States was associated with savings, generated by changes in practice that decreased use of skilled nursing facility care without affecting mortality.

the bundled payments for medical condition program was associated with lower total episode spending, lower spending at skilled nursing facilities, and higher spending on home health care at three years.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the BPCI program on hospital and post-acute care spending, quality of care, and mortality.
the impact of the introduction of a new payment model for hospital care, namely bundled payments for medical episodes of care, on the quality of care, the costs of care and patient outcomes.
the question whether a bundled payment system for medical conditions can be implemented without affecting the quality of care.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of the study support the conclusion that the bundled payment program for acute myocardial Infarction, congestion heart failure, chronic Obstructive pulmonary disease, and pneumonia in the United States was associated with savings and that the savings were generated by the practice changes that decreased the use of high intensity post-acute care after hospital discharge, without affecting quality.

BPCI is associated with a decrease of total episode spending of 1.2% (95% confidence interval, −2.3 to −0.3%) and a decrease in SNF spending of 6.3% (95% CI, −10.0 to −2.7%), without an increase in mortality.
the results of this study are inconclusive and that the study should be repeated with larger sample sizes and with longer follow-up times to determine whether the results are robust.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bundled payment program for medical conditions in BPCI is associated with savings at the 3 year mark without affecting quality.
bundled payment is a viable alternative to fee for service.
the longer term evaluation of BPCI showed that participation in the bundles for medical conditions was associated savings and no changes in mortality at three years.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bundled payment program has been effective at lowering costs without compromising quality.
the BPCI program was associated with a reduction in total episode spending and a reduction in spending for skilled nursing facilities.

the BPCI initiative has had some positive impact on the quality and cost of care for patients with acute myocardial infraction, congestive heart disease, chronic obstructive lung disease, and pneumonia.
